newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan MPs reject bid to sack premier - again.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan MPs reject bid to sack premier - again.

text.p: Taiwan's parliament on Friday rejected -- for third time in a week -- an opposition-led motion that would have urged the president to sack Premier Lien Chan in a bitter row over Lien's ability to fight crime.
The main opposition Democratic Progressive Party said after the motion's defeat that it would temporarily halt the bid, citing concerns for social stability.
"We will not raise the motion in the near term in consideration of social stability," Democratic Progressive deputy John Lee told Reuters by telephone.
"This does not mean we will give up the bid completely. We will raise the motion again when the time is right," Lee said.
Similar non-binding resolutions were voted down by narrow margins on May 9 and 13.
The island's hypersensitive stock market has been hard hit since Monday because of jitters over Taiwan's deeply unsettled domestic politics.

Share prices have plunged seven percent since April 28 when the market entered a correction that many analysts believe was triggered in part by revelations about the kidnap, torture and murder of a television celebrity's teenage daughter.
Lien and his cabinet have come under fierce criticism in recent weeks over a spate of violent crimes that investigators have seemed at a loss to solve.

They include the gangland-style execution of a county magistrate and seven others in his home and an opposition party leader's murder, as well as the kidnap-murder of 17-year-old Pai Hsiao-yen, daughter of TV hostess Pai Ping-ping.

Lien has steadfastly resisted calls for his own head, but said on Monday would step down once an ongoing revision of the constitution is completed, likely in July. He also announced a modest cabinet reshuffle on Wednesday.
President Lee Teng-hui affirmed Lien's intent to resign in July at a news conference on Thursday.
